identify.acting: the person conducting this conversation, for test-client
identify.counterparty: chhoto — the seller, and the company that owns the target
identify.confidentiality: normal confidentiality practices; this is an open source repo

situation.subject: a url shortener
situation.structure: an asset purchase — the buyer is buying the software itself, not the company that owns it; the buyer says the repo will be removed as a public repo

background.claim_sources: a url for the repo, and a readme file describing what chhoto says it does
background.known: it seems functional, but the buyer is not sure how well it follows current standards and practices

assessment.paying_for: the working code — it will run internal to the buyer's own system, so the buyer does not care about the user base
assessment.price_movers: unreliable code (the buyer's example: poor error handling), and obsolete implementation — especially if it generates shortened urls that break on some browsers or OSs
assessment.walk_away: the same grounds as would move the price — unreliable or obsolete code; the buyer says that if the audit finds the code is one of those things badly enough, that ends the deal rather than just moving the price

recommendation.scope: Readme.md only as the claim source; the repo is the codebase against which the claims are checked — the readme is the seller's claim, the code is the evidence
recommendation.deliverable: a report of findings, read against the code inside the window before the repo goes private
recommendation.seller_questions: None — the buyer wants nothing put to the seller directly before closing

notes: the buyer initially declined to state the price, then volunteered around $50k when asked about deal structure
the buyer noted the repo will be removed as a public repo once the deal is done; the deliverable is to be checked against the code within the 14-day window before that happens
the buyer's first answer on the deliverable, 'usual report', was not accepted as field content; the recorded answer is their later words, 'a report of findings'
